card.name: Small words in label sentence openings
card.fires_on: The small words "as" or "to" right after "used", "shown" or at the start of a sentence in drug-label warnings, where a phrase like "as recommended" or "to be" follows.

modes.label: as after used
modes.description: The word "as" after "used", leading into "as recommended" or "as an adjunct".
modes.example: .2 Life-Threatening Respiratory Depression Serious, life-threatening, or fatal respiratory depression has been reported with the use of opioids, even when used<< as>> recommended. Respiratory depression, if not

modes.label: to after shown
modes.description: The word "to" after "has been shown", leading into a finding such as "to be embryotoxic".
modes.example: resulted in severe abnormalities of liver function tests. Carboplatin Injection may cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman. Carboplatin has been shown<< to>> be embryotoxic and teratogenic in

modes.label: As opening a sentence
modes.description: Sentence-initial "As" in "As with any NSAIDs" after a section heading.
modes.example: the drug to the mother. Pediatric Use Safety and effectiveness of ibuprofen tablets in pediatric patients have not been established. Geriatric Use<< As>> with any NSAIDs, caution should be

card.writes: It lowers words like "represent" and "reflects", so the next word is not one of those.
card.plain: It marks little linking words like "as" in "used as recommended" in label text.
